The Keyport Logistics and Technical Support In-House Engineering Services (ISE) is responsible for the Technical Authority functions and Integrated Product Support (IPS) for Combat and Weapon Systems for submarine sonar, combat systems, Navy training systems, integrated Undersea Warfare (USW) systems, and assigned surface and warfare systems. Functional responsibilities encompass Integrated Product Support, Technical Data Management, Advanced Training Systems and Processes, Help Desk Support, Distance Support, Fleet Engineering Support, Information Assurance Support, Material Obsolescence Management, and Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Integration and Supportability. Life-cycle systems support services include engineering and technical support, system performance analysis, supply support, logistics support, configuration management, industrial process controls, training, project management, system performance analysis and monitoring, system troubleshooting and problem resolution, development of engineering changes to maintain or enhance system capabilities and operational availability. Projects supported include CV-TSC, USW- Decision Support System (UWS-DSS), Countermeasures, Aviation Maintenance Training Continuum Systems AMTCS, Heavyweight Torpedo, Lightweight Torpedo, Vertical Launch Anti-Submarine Rocket (VLA), Targets, and Submarine Towed Systems or similar systems. The contractor shall perform the majority of services outlined in the attached Statement of Work (SOW) within the local commuting area of NUWC Division, Keyport. However, some services identified in Section 4 sub-paragraphs require support within the local commuting area of various fleet locations throughout the United States. Any specific work efforts where government facilities are different from the above are outlined in the descriptions of the work in paragraph 4. description: Le maître d'ouvrage souhaite disposer d'une assistance générale à la définition et la mise en oeuvre de la concertation avec les habitants du territoire et l'animation du collectif des élus communautaires tout au long de la mandature. L'assistance portera sur la définition des stratégies, des modalités, des moyens des différentes formes de dialogues et d'animation et leurs mises en oeuvre. La première étape de la mission consistera à proposer une vision d'ensemble du déploiement d'une stratégie de concertation/animation des 4 grandes cibles du projet - les élus, l'administration, les citoyens, les acteurs sociaux-économiques. Le prestataire devra expliciter les intentions, les méthodes, les moyens, un agenda sur le moyen terme. Plusieurs outils de concertation seront mobilisables pour déployer la stratégie de concertation : l'enquête audiovisuelle, l'enquête large spectre administrée par les habitants, les réunions publiques, les ateliers techniques, la création et diffusion de contenus sur les réseaux sociaux, la création, animation et diffusion de débats au format plateau TV. Il appartiendra au prestataire de les mobiliser en fonction de la stratégie proposée. L'accord-cadre sera exécuté par l'émission de bons de commande. Les prestations sont réglées par des prix unitaires. Le montant maximum est de 800 000 euro(s) HT pour la durée de l'accord-cadre

title: Utilities Privatization of the Water System at U.S. Army Garrison-Hawaii (USAG-HI), Island of Oahu, HI
description: DLA Energy, in conjunction with the United States Army, plans to offer the privatization of the water (NAICS 221310) utility system at U.S. Army Garrison -Hawaii (USAG-HI), Island of Oahu, Hawaii. USAG-HI is considering the potential privatization of the water utility systems serving Schofield Barracks � Main Post, Wheeler Army Airfield, Schofield Barracks � East Range, Pililaau Army Recreation Center, Fort Shafter, Tripler Army Medical Center, Fort DeRussy, Helemano Military Reservation, Kahuku Training Area, Aliamanu Military Reservation, and Makua Valley Training Area. The USAG-HI water utility systems to be privatized under this solicitation may include the housing portions of the water utility systems. Utilities Privatization (UP) is defined as the transfer of ownership and responsibility to a municipal, private, regional, district, or cooperative utility company or other entity, for the operations, maintenance, repair, future upgrades, and future utility systems replacements. The conveyance may consist of all right, title, and interest of the United States in the utility system. UP will be accomplished in accordance with 10 U.S.C. �2688 � Utility Systems: Conveyance Authority. As a result of this solicitation, the Contractor will be selected to assume ownership of the water utility system. The new owner shall operate and maintain the system and provide utility services to the Government. Any resulting contract, if awarded, will require the Contractor to furnish all facilities, labor, materials, tools, and equipment necessary to own, maintain, and operate the utility system. All responsibility for maintaining reliable service, including such items as environmental compliance, maintenance costs, major system renovations, construction, equipment, manpower, and overhead costs shall become the utility system owner�s responsibility. The Contractor shall manage the maintenance, repairs, replacement, etc., of the system to ensure continuous, adequate, and dependable service for each Government or tenant connection within the service area. The Contractor shall be responsible for funding all capital investments required to acquire, maintain, and operate the utility system in a safe, reliable condition and to meet the requirements listed in the contract. Real property interests will be conveyed in the form of a Right to Access or an Easement as a reference to the resultant contract. The utility system will be conveyed via a Bill of Sale after a transition period to be determined by the Contractor. Past performance information from potential offerors shall be submitted as directed in the solicitation. title: France – Motion picture and video tape production and related services – Prestations de réalisations audiovisuelles promotionnelles et institutionnelles au profit de l'ISAE-SUPAERO
description: Réalisation et production de vidéos de qualité professionnelle, intégrant toutes les étapes de production, de la conception et rédaction du scénario à la post-production, en passant par le tournage. Ces vidéos seront diffusées sur tous supports digitaux (internet, réseaux sociaux, …) et sur écrans à l'occasion de manifestions publiques (salons, colloques, réunions…). La durée approximative des vidéos sera déterminée lors des réunions préalables avec le Service Communication de l'ISAE-SUPAERO. Deux missions sont à exclure : - La production audiovisuelle de supports pédagogiques innovants de type MOOC (vidéo pour formation en ligne certifiante) ; - Les prestations liées à la technique événementielle, intégrant les étapes de mise à disposition de régie audiovisuelle, de structure scénique, de personnels pour la réalisation et la production de manifestations événementielles (Cérémonie de remise de diplômes en présentiel ou distanciel, webinaires, colloques, etc.). Le détail des missions confiées au titulaire figure au cahier des charges. L'accord-cadre sera exécuté par l'émission de bons de commande lors de la survenance du besoin. Les prestations sont réglées par des prix unitaires

title: Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) - Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO)
description: 20 July 2026 Update 1. CSO procedures have been updated, 20 July 2026. 2. Capability Program Executive, C2 Information Network (CPE C2IN) and Army Contracting Command- Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG) will be conducting an Industry Day on a forthcoming Call for Solutions (CFS) for NGC2 Scalable Software Applications on Thursday, 23 July 2026 11:00 AM EST. Link to join event: https://usg01.safelinks.protection.office365.us/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdod.teams.microsoft.us%2Fl%2Fmeetup-join%2F19%253adod%253ameeting_673603dad2ac405f8468ad9d5ccb6250%2540thread.v2%2F0%3Fcontext%3D%257b%2522Tid%2522%253a%2522fae6d70f-954b-4811-92b6-0530d6f84c43%2522%252c%2522Oid%2522%253a%2522a4e25b63-4741-4856-a1da-622a11a49d14%2522%252c%2522IsBroadcastMeeting%2522%253atrue%257d&data=05%7C02%7Cglen.r.gearhart2.civ%40army.mil%7C4165c88311c3437c39f508dee653c8e2%7Cfae6d70f954b481192b60530d6f84c43%7C0%7C0%7C639201444683482737%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=jZSFMiuuaD32bMiAguWv6CZDGMTQ6dz%2F8%2F3LO9zc4Ls%3D&reserved=0 3. ACC C2 mailbox has been added for engagements with industry. For escalation / issues please contact Eric.J.Roberts48.civ@army.mil. _________________________________________ Command and Control (C2) is foundational to warfighting, and lessons learned from recent support to contingency operations in Ukraine and Israel, as well as threat assessments in the INDOPACOM AoR, show that the Army�s current C2 information systems should be modernized to meet commanders� needs for large scale combat operations against near peer adversaries. Current mission command systems are not mobile, intuitive, or survivable enough to easily overcome the current threat, changes in the character of warfare, and the pace of technology. As part of the Army�s continuous transformation effort, initiatives are being implemented to transform how the Army operates, trains, and equips for C2 capabilities that enhance its lethality, mobility, and survivability in large-scale combat as part of the Joint Force. The Army�s operational imperative is to improve systems responsibly, using innovative solutions from units and industry; at the same time, preparing for the future by ensuring the next generation of C2 systems are built on a portfolio of capabilities that effectively address emerging threats and ensure dominance over adversaries. The Army�s Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) portfolio of capabilities will provide commanders with the ability to make more, better, and faster decisions through advanced analytics, an integrated data layer, open architecture, and robust and resilient transport. The result is data-centric C2 at every echelon that can operate in any environment. NGC2 requirements are currently being informed by persistent experimentation. Market research and prototyping will create a competitive environment for innovative industry partnerships and continuous integration of new technologies. Army Contracting Command- Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG) in support of the Program Executive Office Command, Control, Communications and Network (PEO C3N) and the Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) program is publishing this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), W15P7T-25-S-0001, in accordance with the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement Subpart 212.70 for the purpose of establishing a streamlined vehicle to award innovative C2 capability and functionality. This CSO will remain open until 16 May 2027. This CSO will be open until canceled by the U.S. Army. Proposals shall only be submitted in response to a Request for White Paper (RWP). *********************************************** *Please note: Supplementary documents pertaining to NGC2 is located on the Joint Communications Marketplace (JCM) at https://jtnc.experience.crmforce.mil/JTNC/s/login/, go to �More Communities,� click �Army,� and then �Next Gen Command & Control (NGC2).� The Reading Room is accessed by a link on the NGC2 home page menu. If you have not registered for JCM, please use the following link <https://jtnc.experience.crmforce.mil/JTNC/s/register>. If you have registered for JCM, but need access specifically to NGC2 Community page, you must register for access to this space. Please use the following link and register specifically for NGC2 Community Page https://jtnc.experience.crmforce.mil/JTNC/s/register . You will need a Joint Certification Program (JCP) number and Data Custodian to enter the NGC2 community and view CUI documents. If you do not already have a JCP Certification number, please follow the direction below. To gain access to CUI documents, your company/entity must be certified by the Joint Certification Program (JCP). Your entity/company�s Data Custodian requester (designated) on block 3A of the DD Form 2345 is the only authorized individual that can download the controlled attachment. Your entity/company is responsible for the protection of the controlled document after the download. If your entity/company is not pre-certified by the JCP, you will need to apply for certification by completing a DD Form 2345 and emailing it to jcp-admin@dla.mil. Detailed information regarding the JCP application procedures is available at the JCP website at https://www.dla.mil/Logistics-Operations/Services/JCP/. The ESI Directorate and the Army Contracting Command (ACC) will not review the JCP application or issue the JCP certification. No exceptions will be made to vendors who are not certified in the JCP for the release of the controlled documents. Please direct any questions regarding the JCP certification process to jcp-admin@dla.mil.

De werkelijke omvang van de opdracht kan dus in positieve of negatieve zin afwijken van de genoemde indicatie. Een doelmatige periodieke rapportage van de uitgevoerde activiteiten behoort eveneens tot de scope. De gemeente verwacht van de te contracteren partij dat ingespeeld wordt op nieuwe ontwikkelingen en wijzigingen in wet- en regelgeving. Deze partij communiceert bijvoorbeeld proactief wanneer invordering in meerdere/nieuwe landen mogelijk wordt. De te contracteren partij verstuurt de NHA’s, waarbij de vormgeving in samenwerking met de gemeente tot stand komt, o.a. dat op de uitgeschreven NHA’s verwezen naar de uitvoerende partij voor de bezwaarmogelijkheden, dit dient in tekst en d.m.v. een QR duidelijk te worden. De gemeente zorgt ervoor dat op haar website verwezen wordt naar de bezwaarmogelijkheden bij opdrachtnemer. De gemeente is op zoek naar een partij die een snelle en efficiënte afhandeling van de invorderingsdossiers en bezwarencases kan borgen, waarbij klantvriendelijkheid hoog in het vaandel staat. Wetende dat niemand ‘blij’ wordt van een naheffing, is juist bij de klantcontacten een klantvriendelijke en waar nodig de-escalerende benadering voor de gemeente van belang. De gemeente Breda is momenteel bezig met het opstellen van een wielklembeleid. Momenteel is de gemeente bezig met de eerste onderzoekende fase. Het is mogelijk dat tijdens het contract of net voor het vastleggen van het contract meer informatie beschikbaar is over het invoeren van het wielklembeleid. title: Netherlands – Postal services – Postdienstverlening
description: Procedure Aanbesteding middels de Europees openbare procedure conform de (gewijzigde) aanbestedingswet 2012. Opdrachtgever De opdrachtgever bij deze aanbesteding is de Gemeente Breda. Voor meer informatie over de Gemeente Breda verwijzen wij u naar de website van de gemeente: www.breda.nl. Scope van de opdracht De opdracht omvat de integrale postdienstverlening voor de gemeente Breda, waaronder in ieder geval: het ophalen, sorteren, vervoeren en bezorgen van geadresseerde poststukken; het ophalen, sorteren, vervoeren en bezorgen van pakketten; het verwerken en bezorgen van verkiezingspost; het verwerken van retourzendingen; Haalservice (postbus)post en Brengservcie (postbus)post; het verzorgen van aangetekende poststukken (Binnenland en Buitenland) en overige bijzondere postdiensten; het verzorgen van kwaliteitsborging en prestatiemonitoring. De exacte omvang en inhoud van de dienstverlening zijn nader uitgewerkt in het Programma van Eisen en de SLA. Buiten de scope valt: verspreiding huis aan huis berichten (gemeentelijke berichten) en fietskoersdiensten. Percelen Deze opdracht is niet verdeeld in percelen. Doel Het afsluiten van een raamovereenkomst met één contractpartij voor het verzorgen van de postdienstverlening ten behoeve van gemeente Breda. Deze raamovereenkomst zal worden aangegaan voor een periode van 2 jaar. De ingangsdatum van deze raamovereenkomst is 1 februari 2027. De opdrachtgever heeft bij wederzijds goedvinden van partijen het recht deze raamovereenkomst tegen dezelfde voorwaarden en condities twee (2) maal te verlengen, telkens voor de duur van één (1) jaar. De maximale looptijd van de raamovereenkomst bedraagt derhalve vier (4) jaar. De besluitvorming ten aanzien van deze verlenging(en) geschiedt op basis van evaluatie van de geleverde prestaties van de dienstverlening. Gunning en motivatie De aanbestedende dienst gunt de opdracht aan de inschrijver op basis van het gunningscriterium laagste prijs, omdat de gevraagde dienstverlening volledig, objectief en eenduidig is gespecificeerd in het Programma van Eisen, de Service Level Agreement (SLA) en de raamovereenkomst. De vereiste kwaliteit van de dienstverlening is volledig vastgelegd in minimumeisen, prestatie-eisen, KPI's en contractvoorwaarden ten aanzien van onder meer bezorgkwaliteit, bestelkwaliteit, verkiezingspost, klachtenafhandeling, managementrapportages, continuïteit, traceerbaarheid, informatiebeveiliging en duurzaamheid. Alle inschrijvers dienen onvoorwaardelijk aan deze eisen te voldoen. De aanbestedende dienst is van oordeel dat inschrijvers zich hierdoor niet wezenlijk op kwaliteit kunnen onderscheiden zonder af te wijken van de gestelde eisen. Aanbestedende dienst is voornemens de opdracht te gunnen aan de inschrijver die een geldige inschrijving heeft ingediend en de laagste totale inschrijfprijs heeft aangeboden. Maximale contractwaarde De maximale opdrachtwaarde in het kader van deze overeenkomst wordt gesteld op € 2.000.000,- bezien over de looptijd van de overeenkomst, inclusief verlengingsopties. Aan het genoemde bedrag kunnen geen rechten worden ontleend. Voor opdrachtgever geldt geen afnameverplichting. Mocht gedurende de looptijd van de raamovereenkomst de maximale opdrachtwaarde worden overschreden dan zal de raamovereenkomst (eerder) worden beëindigd. Mercell Deze aanbesteding zal uitsluitend en geheel digitaal online worden afgehandeld via het Mercell platform (www.mercell.com). Een uitgebreide instructie met betrekking tot digitaal aanbesteden treft u aan in de Vragenlijsten.

description: La présente procédure a pour objet de confier à un concessionnaire de service public l'exploitation du camping de Strasbourg. Situé à la montagne verte, le camping de Strasbourg fait l'objet d'un classement 4 étoiles depuis son ouverture en 2015. L'équipement est, à ce jour, constitué de 92 hébergements locatifs (35 HLL, 24 mobil-homes, 29 tentes toiles et bois, 4 roulottes), de 86 emplacements libres ainsi que d'un espace camping-cars de 19 emplacements, d'une aire de jeux et d'une piscine chauffée, d'un centre de vie, de deux sanitaires, d'une laverie, d'un bar /restaurant, d'une borne pour camping-cars. Entre le 1er octobre 2024 et le 30 septembre 2025, le camping de Strasbourg a enregistré 134 505 nuitées (69 541 en camping et 64 964 en hébergements locatifs) Le camping restera ouvert et accessible 24h sur 24, tous les jours, y compris les dimanches et jours fériés. Le futur concessionnaire sera chargé d'assurer la gestion des installations, l'amélioration et le développement de l'offre de services visant, entre autre, à conserver le classement 4 étoiles ainsi que l'obtention du label « Accueil Vélo ». Outre la gestion et l'exploitation, le concessionnaire devra assurer également la promotion du camping et de son territoire, l'entretien, la maintenance, la sécurité et la surveillance de l'équipement. En matière d'hébergements, il assurera le remplacement des hébergements locatifs actuels (hors chalets HLL) tout en répondant aux tendances actuelles du marché, ainsi que les travaux de rénovation/maintenance des chalets HLL existants. Tous les travaux immobiliers seront portés par lui dans l'objectif, notamment, de rénover l'ancien bâtiment d'accueil en logements pour saisonniers et salle de séminaire, de doter le site des installations techniques et moyens d'exploitation indispensables à la gestion de l'activité avec la création de locaux pour accueillir un atelier, des garages et des lieux de stockage en dur, sécurisés et fermés. Il devra également réaliser des travaux portant sur divers équipements : installation de bornes de recharges, aménagement d'une cuisine équipée professionnelle, renouvellement complet du mobilier de restauration, rénovation et entretien des aménagements extérieurs (aires de pique- nique et de jeu…) et aménagement paysagers. Le concessionnaire veillera, de manière générale, à l'optimisation de la gestion énergétique de l'ensemble des installations du site. Le concessionnaire collectera la taxe de séjour auprès des usagers. Il tirera sa rémunération de l'exploitation du service et assumera l'ensemble des charges résultant des missions qui lui sont confiées au titre du contrat. Il exploitera le service public à ses risques et périls sur la base d'un compte d'exploitation prévisionnel établi pour toute la durée du contrat (soit 10 ans) et annexé au futur contrat. En outre, en contrepartie de la mise à disposition des ouvrages, le Concessionnaire versera chaque année au Concédant une redevance fixe et/ou variable. Les tarifs seront fixés par l'Eurométropole de Strasbourg

Dabei teilt sich die Prüfung von KVA in zwei unterschiedliche Arten von Prüfungen auf: - Die automatisierte Grundprüfung wird bei jedem KVA ausschließlich systemisch durchgeführt. - Die manuelle Tiefenprüfung findet aufbauend auf der automatisierten Grundprüfung für bestimmte Fahrzeuge statt. Für die Prüfung von KVA und der Abgleich der Proformarechnungen sowie deren Freigabe stellt der Auftragnehmer ein Webportal in seinem System als digitalen Arbeitsplatz zur Verfügung, über den Fachbetriebe ihre KVA, sonstige Unterlagen und Proformarechnungen hochladen und ihre Konditionen verwalten können. Gleichzeitig kann der Auftraggeber in diesem Webportal die von ihm notwendigen Prüfungen, Abgleiche und Freigaben durchführen. Perspektivisch sind die freigegebenen KVA ggf. zusammen mit den notwendigen Unterlagen dem Auftraggeber über eine Schnittstelle im zukünftigen System des Auftraggebers zur Verfügung zu stellen.

title: Germany – Business development consultancy services – IuK-gestützte Kommunikationsdienstleistungen Bürgerdialog
description: Der AN unterstützt den AG bei der Kommunikation mit Bürgern (Bürgerdialog) und anderen Zielgruppen zu Themen, die in die Zuständigkeit des BMWE fallen mit Hilfe von Hotlines und über die allgemeine Behördennummer 115. Der AN nimmt alle „Inboundgespräche“ (eingehende Anrufe) der Hotlines und die weitergeleiteten Anrufe der einheitlichen Behördennummer 115 (2nd Level) entgegen. Diese sind professionell (schnell, verständlich, höflich) und mit qualitativ hochwertiger Beratungstiefe (kompetent, inhaltlich richtig) in deutscher Sprache zu beantworten. Sofern notwendig, beantwortet der AN Bürgeranfragen durch das Führen von „Outboundgesprächen“ (abgehende Anrufe) oder schriftlich und bietet computergestützte, geführte Hilfestellung bei der Navigation auf der BMWE-Website mit Bezug zur Beratung (Co-Browsing). Der Leistungsgegenstand umfasst Grundleistungen, die sich an den bisherigen Erfahrungswerten und Leistungsanforderungen orientieren und im Folgenden beschrieben werden: AP 1: Hotline Mittelstand und Existenzgründung AP 2: Einheitliche Behördennummer 115 AP 3: Ad-hoc Hotline (Option)

title: Netherlands – Services in connection with motion-picture and video-tape production – Video en animatie
description: De Gemeente Den Haag is voornemens een Raamovereenkomst af te sluiten voor het leveren van video-, animatie- en aanverwante audiovisuele productiediensten ten behoeve van de gehele gemeentelijke organisatie. De gemeente zet audiovisuele middelen in voor uiteenlopende communicatievraagstukken, waaronder publiekscommunicatie, participatie, voorlichting, arbeidsmarktcommunicatie, interne communicatie, evenementen, bestuurlijke communicatie en campagnevoering. De opdracht is verdeeld in twee percelen: Perceel 1 – Integrale video- en animatieproducties Perceel 1 omvat het ontwikkelen, produceren en opleveren van integrale audiovisuele producties. Hieronder vallen onder andere: conceptontwikkeling; redactie en scripting; videoproducties; animaties en motion graphics; productie en regie; montage en postproductie; ondertiteling en toegankelijkheidsvoorzieningen; livestreams en registraties. De werkzaamheden kunnen variëren van korte videoproducties tot omvangrijke campagne-, voorlichtings- en bestuurlijke producties. Voor dit perceel worden maximaal drie opdrachtnemers gecontracteerd. Perceel 2 – Flexibele productiecapaciteit (brokerconstructie) Perceel 2 omvat het leveren en organiseren van flexibele productiecapaciteit via een brokerconstructie. De opdrachtnemer is verantwoordelijk voor het beschikbaar stellen, matchen en coördineren van externe makers en productieprofessionals, waaronder: camjo's; videomakers; editors; contentmakers; overige audiovisuele specialisten. De broker fungeert als centraal aanspreekpunt voor de gemeente en is verantwoordelijk voor de beschikbaarheid, matching, kwaliteitsborging en administratieve afhandeling van de inzet van deze flexibele capaciteit. Perceel 2 is bedoeld voor de tijdelijke inzet van individuele audiovisuele professionals ter ondersteuning van de gemeentelijke organisatie en niet voor het uitvragen van integrale productieopdrachten. Voor dit perceel wordt één opdrachtnemer gecontracteerd.

title: Provision of Audience Research Services
description: The Board of Trustees for the National Galleries of Scotland ("NGS") wish to award a Contract for the Provision of Audience Research Services. The Service Provider is required to conduct Audience Research to provide insight and analysis about our visitors in order to support the Organisation’s 2030 Strategy, Business Plan and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), special projects and inform organisation-wide strategic planning. The Service Provider shall be a member of, accredited by, or operate in accordance with the standards, codes of conduct and professional requirements of the Market Research Society (MRS) or an equivalent recognised professional body for market research, social research, insight or analytics. This Contract shall primarily provide Fieldwork Surveys and associated Project Management, Client Data Access, Analysis and Reporting for each of our four gallery sites. Services will be agreed to on an “as required” basis with no commitment to a minimum volume of work. NGS may, at its absolute discretion, require the Service Provider to provide Audience Research Services at this fifth site, currently under construction, at any time during the Contract term. If permitted by applicable procurement legislation, where additional audience research requirements arise during the Contract term that constitute an extension of the Services, NGS reserves the right to procure such additional services from the Service Provider. For full details of the Contract Requirements please refer to the associated Tender and Contract Documents. The Service Provider must have a clear understanding of the contract requirements and the organisational needs of NGS. As part of the tender exercise, the Service Provider must detail a robust and flexible methodology for conducting Audience Research Services that will meet all data capture requirements. There is no commitment to a minimum spend over the duration of the Contract. Under this Contract, no minimum spend is guaranteed. The agreement will be non-exclusive i.e. NGS reserves the right, in certain, circumstances, to procure out with the Contract Agreement, as and when required. In the event of unsatisfactory performance by the successful Service Provider and the termination of the contract by either party, NGS reserves the right to negotiate the continuance of the services with the second and third placed Service Providers.

description: Les besoins en synoptiques pour la DSAR: Le développement d'une représentation standardisée des stations locales (noeuds de gestion, stations de pompage ou de prétraitement) présente de multiples intérêts : -Faciliter la compréhension du fonctionnement des sites pour les nouveaux arrivants -Faciliter les échanges entre agents de terrain et de bureau -Limiter les risques de confusion lors de la programmation des interventions dans les réseaux -Faciliter le travail avec des intervenants extérieurs ne connaissant pas les installations Concrètement, les synoptiques répondront à plusieurs usages et notamment : -Fournir une représentation unique de chaque ouvrage, qui sera utilisée à la fois comme fond de vue Supervision, et dans les Fiches de Fonctionnement, documents en cours d'élaboration qui définiront, pour chaque station locale, son mode de fonctionnement dans toutes les situations (temps sec/ de pluie, basses eaux/ crue, mode normal/ dégradé ...) -Fournir un support de formation, pour les régulateurs du PC SAPHYRS ou d'autres agents DSAR, ou d'autres Directions -Repérage sur site à l'aide de supports placardés localement, ou réalisation de classeurs qui seront mis à disposition des agents de terrain dans les véhicules d'intervention -Illustration dans les documents et notes élaborées par la DSAR Différents types de synoptiques Différents types de synoptiques seront nécessaires pour chaque ouvrage, en fonction de sa complexité, de sa criticité, et des spécificités qu'il présente : -Synoptique 2D très simplifié pour une compréhension immédiate et globale du fonctionnement -Synoptique 2D plus élaboré pour rentrer dans certains détails -Synoptique 3D &quot; statique &quot; : des vues 3D figées sous des angles pertinents pédagogiquement -Maquette 3D : fichier informatique qui permet de regarder l'ouvrage sous différents angles, de générer des vues (coupes, plans ...) selon ses besoins -Synoptique animé : sur une vue 2D ou 3D, représentation symbolique et dynamique des écoulements pour faciliter la compréhension des ouvrages les plus complexes. Un rendu homogène L'homogénéité des rendus est importante, pour assurer une bonne compréhension de tous les intervenants, sur les Unités d'Intervention Est et Ouest, mais également en Central, pour les agents du PC SAPHYRS, de l'Unité Méthodes et Ordonnancement, ou pour des partenaires d'autres Directions comme la Direction Technique, dont les projets sont souvent interfacés avec la DSAR. Ainsi, tous les synoptiques d'un même type (2D simplifié, 3D etc.) seront être homogènes pour tous les ouvrages représentés. Et pour chaque ouvrage, la cohérence sera cruciale entre les différents synoptiques qui apportent différents niveaux de compréhension et de détail. Le pilotage du projet Synoptiques sera assuré par l'Unité Méthodes et Ordonnancement du Service Exploitation et Maintenance de la DSAR. Le premier marché a permis d'établir la charte graphique commune à tous les synoptiques, et de réaliser les premiers synoptiques. Le travail doit se poursuivre pour traiter tous les sites de la DSAR nécessitant une représentation graphique

Dynamisch aankoopsysteem De hierbij gebruikte procedure is het Dynamisch Aankoopsysteem uit de Aanbestedingswet 2012. De procedure verloopt volledig elektronisch via het online aanbestedingsplatform Negometrix. Een Dynamisch aankoopsysteem (DAS) is een elektronisch proces voor het doen van gangbare aankopen van werken, leveringen of diensten, waarvan de kenmerken wegens de algemene beschikbaarheid op de markt voldoen aan onze behoeften. Doelstelling DAS De doelstelling van het DAS is een zo groot mogelijke groep kwalitatief goede ondernemingen toe te laten zonder de beheersbaarheid te verliezen. Op deze manier creëert Defensie een optimale marktwerking, waarbij Defensie kwalitatief optimale Producten kan selecteren tegen zo laag mogelijke kosten, binnen de gewenste levertijden. Het MatlogCo beoogt hiermee op een eerlijke wijze, snel en eenvoudig haar behoeften op te vullen, door middel van volledige concurrentiestelling. Werking van het Dynamisch aankoopsysteem in het kort Voor deze aanbesteding volgt Defensie de Europese aanbestedingsprocedure 'Dynamisch aankoopsysteem', conform de Aanbestedingswet. Hierbij wordt onderscheid gemaakt naar twee fasen: 1. Instellingsfase 2. Gunningsfase Deze fasen worden nader uitgewerkt in vragenlijst 1.1. Kort samengevat Gegadigde dient een Verzoek tot toelating in; Als Gegadigde aan de gestelde eisen voldoet en er geen uitsluitingsgronden van toepassing zijn, wordt zij als Deelnemer toegelaten. Toelating tot het DAS houdt geen opdracht in; Het MatlogCo plaats een nadere uitvraag; Deelnemer schrijft in; Het MatlogCo beoordeelt de Inschrijvingen en gunt aan de economisch meest voordelige Inschrijving. Looptijd van het Dynamisch aankoopsysteem Bij de publicatie in maart 2023 had het Dynamisch Aankoopsysteem (DAS) een initiële looptijd van 48 maanden. Echter, aangezien deze DAS een voortzetting is van de vorige DAS met het negometrix nummer 210681, resteert er nu nog een looptijd van 35 maanden. Het is belangrijk op te merken dat de Aanbestedende Dienst de looptijd één keer kan verlengen, met een periode van 48 maanden. Het staat de Aanbestedende dienst vrij om aan het DAS gedurende de looptijd producten en/of kwalificaties toe te voegen of te verwijderen. Dit zal de Aanbestedende dienst waar nodig aankondigen met een rectificatie.

description: Istekki Oy pyytää osallistumishakemuksia dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään (DPS), jonka kohteena on Digitaaliset asiointipalvelut: Teknologia,- kehitys-, toimitus-, tukipalvelu-, asiantuntijapalvelu-, konsultointi- ja valmisratkaisut sekä alusta- ja lisenssipalvelut. DPS:n kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin osallistumispyynnössä ja sen liitteissä, erityisesti liitteessä "Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän kohde ja sisältö". Dynaaminen hankintajärjestelmä on jaettu kymmeneen (10) eri koriin (osa-alueeseen): 1. Liferay DXP teknologia ja lisenssit sekä alustapalvelut ja valmisratkaisut 2. Liferay CE teknologia sekä alustapalvelut ja valmisratkaisut 3. Wordpress teknologia ja lisenssit sekä alustapalvelut ja valmisratkaisut 4. Drupal teknologia ja lisenssit sekä alustapalvelut ja valmisratkaisut 5. Mobiilikehitys teknologiat (Google Flutter ja React Native) ja lisenssit sekä alustapalvelut ja valmisratkaisut 6. Matomo analytiikkaohjelmisto, teknologia, lisenssit ja alustapalvelut sekä valmisratkaisut 7. Keycloak -IDM ohjelmisto, teknologiat, lisenssit ja alustapalvelut sekä valmisratkaisut 8. Digitaalisten palveluiden käyttöliittymäsuunnittelu, visuaalinen suunnittelu ja toteutus sekä palvelukonseptointi/brändäys 9. Määrittelemätön hankintakori – tarkentuu myöhemmin 10. Määrittelemätön hankintakori – tarkentuu myöhemmin. Ehdokas voi tässä vaiheessa hakeutua koreihin 1-8. Koreihin 9-10 ei voi perustamisvaiheessa hakeutua. Istekki Oy varaa mahdollisuuden perustaa korit 9-10 dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän voimassaoloaikana. Dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään voivat hakea tarjoajaksi kaikki sellaiset ehdokkaat, jotka täyttävät ESPD-lomakkeella ja osallistumispyynnöllä ilmoitetut soveltuvuusvaatimukset. Dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään hyväksytään kaikki ehdokkaat, jotka täyttävät asetetut soveltuvuusvaatimukset. Kaikki kiinnostuneet ehdokkaat voivat koko dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän keston ajan pyytää oikeutta osallistua dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään. Dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään hyväksyttävien ehdokkaiden määrää ei ole rajoitettu. Ehdokas hakeutuu dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään jättämällä osallistumishakemuksen. Istekki Oy voi halutessaan lyhentää tai pidentää dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän kestoa julkaisemalla siitä hankintailmoituksen. Istekki Oy voi myös korottaa hankinnan arvoa julkaisemalla siitä hankintailmoituksen. Dynaaminen hankintajärjestelmä on perustamisvaiheen jälkeen vuosittain suljettuna heinä- ja joulukuiden ajan. Die Leistungen umfassen die Konzeption, das Projektmanagement, die Redaktion, die Gestaltung, das Lektorat, die Übersetzung und den Satz von Publikationen/Veröffentlichungen sowie die Umsetzung von Video- und Podcastproduktionsleistungen: Los 1: Redaktionelle Kommunikationsdienstleistungen Los 1 umfasst die regelmäßige Erstellung von Beiträgen (Text- und Multimedia) für das Onlinemagazin DAAD Journal, den Newsletter DAAD Aktuell und das zugehörige Projektmanagement. Zudem umfasst Los 1 die redaktionelle und gestalterische Erstellung, das Projektmanagement und die (Neu-)Konzeption des DAAD-Jahresberichts, der DAAD-Außenstellenberichte, des DWIH-Jahresberichts und von GATE-Germany Publikationen. Darüber hinaus können noch weitere Formate und Publikationen über das Los beauftragt werden. Ebenfalls Bestandteil von Los 1 sind Veröffentlichungen im Rahmen von Kampagnen und Sonderprogrammen. Dies umfasst die Formate Print (u. a. Broschüren, Flyer, Postkarten), digital/online (u. a. pdf-Broschüren/Flyer, e-paper, interaktive Broschüren), online (u. a. wissenschaftliche Online-Artikel, Redaktion von Webseiten und Grafiken, Newsletter etc.) sowie Bewegtbildformate (u. a. Videos, animierte Erklärfilme, 360-Grad-Filme, Virtual und Augmented Reality) und Podcast-Produktionen. Es handelt sich hierbei einerseits um Formate für das internationale Forschungsmarketing. Hiermit ist vorrangig - aber nicht ausschließlich - die Initiative "Research in Germany – Land of Ideas" gemeint. Andererseits handelt es sich um die Umsetzung von Veröffentlichungen von Sonderprogrammen – vorrangig, aber nicht ausschließlich – des Programms „Konrad Zuse Schools of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence“. Weiterhin Bestandteil von Los 1 sind die gestalterische und redaktionelle Erstellung des DAAD Alumnimagazins Letter inkl. Multimedia-Formaten und die Übertragung der Magazininhalte in ein bestehendes Online-Format sowie in einen Newsletter. Darüber hinaus beinhaltet Los 1 die Erstellung von Beiträgen (Text- und Video) für die weitere Alumni-Kommunikation , v.a. die Erstellung eines Newsletters für Alumni aus Deutschland. Darüber hinaus können noch weitere Formate und Publikationen der Alumni-Kommunikation über das Los beauftragt werden. Los 2: Grafik- und Design-Leistungen Los 2 umfasst die Pflege und Weiterentwicklung des DAAD-Corporate Designs, die Erstellung von neuen Basislayouts und den Satz und die Befüllung von bestehenden Layouts. Dazu zählen z.B. Publikationen, Factsheets, Power-Points-Präsentationen usw. Nähere Einzelheiten hierzu entnehmen Sie bitte den Leistungsbeschreibungen für die beiden Lose, Anlage BW 2 Los 1 und Anlage BW 2 Los 2.

title: 69--CH-53E Containerized Flight Training Device (CFTD) Baseline Configuration Upgrade (BCU) Pre-Solicitation Teleconference
description: NAWCTSD will host a Pre-solicitation Teleconference (mini-Industry Day) for the CH-53E Baseline Configuration Upgrade (BCU) focused exclusively on the Future Airborne Capability Environment (FACE) Technical Standard. This standard is referenced for the development of software as a part of solicitation N61340-17-R-0035. The pre-solicitation teleconference will take place on Thursday, 06 April 2017 from 1:00 - 3:00 pm EDT. The pre-solicitation teleconference will include a dedicated question and answer period allowing contractors to ask any questions related to the FACE portion of solicitation N61340-17-R-0035. Answers to the questions generated from this pre-solicitation teleconference will be provided to all potential offerors. However, it should be noted that, all questions to the stated solicitation, unrelated to FACE, shall continue to follow normal protocol, with contractors submitting a completed L-1 Question and Answer Form and emailing it to Nicole Knight at Nicole.knight@navy.mil. All interested TSC III Lot II vendors are welcome to call in to this teleconference and should request the dial-in number from NAWCTSD Contracts, Nicole Knight (nicole.knight@navy.mil) no later than 2:30 pm EDT on Wednesday, 05 April 2017. In this request, include your company name, attendees’ names, email addresses, phone numbers, and company address to confirm attendance. Subcontractor requests must be requested through the Prime Contractor. All attendees’ for each company are encouraged to use only one call-in line. The Future Airborne Capability Environment (FACE) Technical Standard is the open avionics standard for making military computing operations more robust, interoperable, portable and secure. The standard enables developers to create and deploy a wide catalog of applications for use across the entire spectrum of military aviation systems through a common operating environment, resulting in lower implementation costs, standards that support a robust architecture and enable quality software development, more capabilities reaching the warfighter faster, and innovation and competition within the avionics industry. FACE is maintained by The Open Group FACE Consortium, a government and industry partnership to define an open avionics environment for all military airborne platform types. The FACE Consortium is a vendor-neutral forum that provides standardized approaches for using open standards with avionics systems. The FACE Consortium works to develop and consolidate FACE open standards, best practices, guidance documents and business models. The Government has included a brief entitled “FACE 101�? for interested contractors to review prior to the teleconference. A NAVAIR Subject Matter Expert (SME) will present this briefing and attendees are encouraged to download the briefing so that they can follow along as he presents the materials. For more information regarding FACE, including the FACE Standards, FACE Data Architecture, The Open Group Architecture Framework Technical Reference Model, and related documentation, please visit the Open Group website at: http://www.opengroup.org/face. Failure of an offeror to call-in to the conference or to submit any questions will be construed to mean that the offeror fully understands all requirements of the solicitation. Prospective offerors are advised that the teleconference will be held solely for the purpose of explaining the FACE Technical Standard as it relates to this solicitation. All prospective offerors are advised that solicitation N61340-17-R-0035 will remain unchanged at the conclusion of the teleconference, unless this solicitation is amended in writing. If an amendment is issued, normal procedures relating to the acknowledgement and receipt of any such amendment shall be applicable. In no event, will failure to attend the conference constitute grounds for a claim after award of the delivery order. title: Notice of Intent for NIH/NIA GraphPad Prism Subscription Renewal
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT, NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. A REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) WILL NOT BE ISSUED AND QUOTES WILL NOT BE REQUESTED. The National Institute of Health National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to award a firm fixed price sole source contract under the authority of FAR 12.102(a), only one source being available to meet the Government's needs, to: GraphPad Software, LLC 225 Franklin St FL 26 Boston, MA, 02110 The NIA hereby submits a notice of intent to award a sole source firm fixed price purchase order for Prism Group Academic Yearly Subscription with 300 activations for their Intramural Research Program (IRP). The Computational Biology and Genomics Core (CBGC) requires a comprehensive, powerful, and user-friendly statistical and graphing software license subscription for the National Institute on Aging (NIA) Intramural Research Program (IRP). Most NIA-IRP research scientists need intuitive statistical and graphing software that integrates seamlessly with Microsoft Excel. Prism offers a familiar, Excel-like interface and is specifically designed for the types of analyses experimental scientists perform. GraphPad Prism tracks and organizes a scientist�s work in a unique way, linking data, graphs, and analyses together. Changes in data automatically update all related analyses and graphs. Prism includes help and teaching information to guide a scientist in choosing a statistical test and creating the appropriate graph. Purchasing an institute-wide license will benefit the majority of experimental scientists at NIA-IRP and be more cost-effective than acquiring individual licenses. NIA-IRP has been using this software since 2006 or earlier. Over the past 5-6 years, CBGC has acquired varying numbers of seats, and there is now a need to purchase 300 seats to meet current demand. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541519. title: Dental and Audiology Coordinator for the Vermont Army National Guard
description: This is a non-personal services contract to provide the Vermont Army National Guard (VTARNG) Deputy State Surgeon?s Office (DSS) with professional, non-clinical administrative support services for the Dental Health Program and the Hearing Conservation Program. The strategic objective of this contract is to optimize the medical, dental, and auditory readiness of VTARNG Service Members (SMs) in accordance with Army Regulation (AR) 40-501 (Standards of Medical Fitness) and AR 40-502 (Medical Readiness). The contractor shall deliver independent, highly accurate administrative data entry, records tracking, scheduling, and metrics reporting as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS).Non-Personal Services Framework In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 37.104, this contract is strictly designated as a non-personal services contract. Government Authority and Supervision: The Government shall not exercise any direct supervision, tasking, or administrative control over contractor employees performing services under this contract. Contractor personnel shall remain at all times under the direct supervision, management, and administrative control of the Contractor?s Contract Manager (CM).Contractor Accountability: The Contractor shall be solely responsible for the selection, hiring, oversight, conduct, scheduling, and performance of its personnel. Contractor employees shall be accountable solely to the Contractor, who, in turn, is responsible to the Government for the successful delivery of the outcomes outlined herein. Professional Boundaries: Under no circumstances shall any relationship resembling an employer-employee (co-employment) relationship be established between the Government and contractor personnel. Service Contract Act (SCA) / Service Contract Labor Standards (SCLS) Compliance To maintain regulatory alignment with 41 U.S.C. Chapter 67 (Service Contract Labor Standards) and to prevent labor misclassification or Wage Determination violations: Mandated Labor Classification: Offerors shall utilize the mandatory SCA labor category of Medical Record Clerk (Labor Category Code 12160) to execute all requirements outlined in this PWS. Wage and Benefit Floor: All proposed labor rates must strictly conform to or exceed the minimum wage and fringe benefit requirements established in the applicable Department of Labor (DOL) Wage Determination attached to this solicitation. Strictly Administrative Scope: The duties outlined under this contract are exclusively clerical, administrative, and data-driven. The Medical Record Clerk is a non-clinical role. Contractor personnel are strictly prohibited from performing any tasks that require clinical evaluation, medical charting, clinical triage, patient counseling, or the independent authoring of medical/dental opinions. Mandatory Personnel Qualifications. The Contractor shall ensure that all personnel assigned to perform services under this contract possess and maintain, at a minimum, the following mandatory professional qualifications: Professional Experience Healthcare Administration Background: A minimum of two (2) years of demonstrated, hands-on experience in medical or dental administration, medical records management, military health administration, or a related healthcare clerical field. Records Management Proficiency: Proven experience handling sensitive personal data, physical/electronic archiving, and verifying the administrative completeness of standardized medical/dental intake documentation. Technical and Computer Skills Microsoft Office Suite: Demonstrated high-level proficiency in using the Microsoft Office Suite, specifically: Microsoft Excel: Ability to manage spreadsheets, utilize basic formulas, and organize data for weekly metrics reporting. Microsoft Word: Ability to draft professional administrative correspondence and schedules. Microsoft Outlook: Ability to coordinate scheduling and professional communication across secure email networks. Systems Adaptability: Proven capability to quickly learn and perform high-accuracy data entry within proprietary military and federal web-based databases (including but not limited to MEDCHART, eCase, DENCLASS, and MEDPROS) following initial Government-provided systems training. Security and Information Assurance Clearance: Federal Clearability: All personnel must be U.S. citizens and must be capable of successfully passing a federal Tier 1 background investigation (formerly National Agency Check with Inquiries - NACI) to secure a Common Access Card (CAC) for physical installation access and logical access to secure military networks. Data Privacy Competency: Prior experience handling Protected Health Information (PHI) and Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in strict compliance with HIPAA, HITECH, and military privacy regulations.

The Government's official, contractually binding responses are detailed below: QUESTION 1: "Thank you for the information. I originally found this solicitation on sam.gov. My question is specifically if your organization intends on awarding multiple Contractors to the BPA contract or do you intend on awarding it to one company. I have seen different agencies do either one." GOVERNMENT RESPONSE: The Government intends to establish only one (1) Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) from this solicitation, with one (1) vendor. Current market research and administrative efficiency evaluations indicate that a single-award BPA is the most advantageous path for this base-wide contingency requirement. The single award will be made to the responsible offeror whose quote represents the Lowest Priced Technically Acceptable (LPTA) offer conforming to the solicitation requirements. QUESTION 2: "As part of our market research and quotation efforts for the temporary cooling requirement at Homestead Air Reserve Base, one of our interested vendors..." "...has requested the opportunity to conduct a site visit to better understand the facility layout and provide the most accurate equipment recommendation and pricing. Would it be possible to arrange a site visit for the vendor? If so, please provide any available dates, times, access procedures, security requirements, and the appropriate point of contact for coordinating entry onto the installation. The vendor has advised that a site walk would help them validate cooling requirements and ensure their proposed solution is properly sized for the space. Thank you for your assistance. I look forward to your guidance on coordinating this request." GOVERNMENT RESPONSE: No, the Government will not host or authorize a pre-award site visit for this solicitation. The professional and contractual rationale for this determination is established as follows: This requirement is being competed under FAR Part 12 (Commercial Products and Commercial Services) to establish a service and equipment rental agreement. The site-visit policies and guidelines cited under FAR Part 36 (including FAR Companion / FC 36.1) apply strictly to Construction contracts and are not legally applicable to simplified commercial equipment lease agreements. This BPA is a base-wide, emergency contingency vehicle. Equipment and support services will be ordered and deployed to various, unspecified facilities across Homestead ARB on an as-needed, temporary basis (e.g., in the event of primary facility HVAC mechanical failure). There is no active physical "HVAC deficit" or single designated project footprint to inspect; consequently, a site walkthrough would yield no representative technical data. Temporary cooling systems on base must connect directly to standard, pre-existing commercial-grade utility connection ports (electrical taps and water quick-connects). Rented hardware must be built to standard commercial configurations capable of interfacing with these standard base interfaces, which are built to standardized tolerances in accordance with UFC 3-410-01 (HVAC Systems). No custom construction or site-specific modifications are authorized under this agreement. The solicitation documents, specifically Attachment 4 (Formal Fillable BPA Price List) and the Statement of Work (SOW), provide precise, comprehensive technical specifications for all forty-plus (40+) line items of equipment and services (including labor, transport, forklift fees, pigtails, and hoses). Industry has successfully competed, priced, and executed this exact scope of services historically at Homestead ARB. Reminder: Quoters are directed to formulate their fully burdened rental rates (which shoud include: delivery, setup, and ancillary connection parts) based solely on the standardized technical specifications detailed in the SOW and the Price List. QUESTION 3: Vendor "...is an interested bidder for the opportunity mentioned in the subject line. We would like to request a site visit, if possible, to obtain additional information and better understand the scope of work. This would allow us to prepare a more accurate and comprehensive quote and ensure that we can perform the required work efficiently. Please let us know if a site visit can be arranged and, if so, the available dates and times." GOVERNMENT RESPONSE: Refer to the Government Response for Question 2. The Government will not host, authorize, or facilitate pre-award site visits or physical facility inspections for this commercial equipment rental services solicitation. All technical scope and pricing parameters are fully defined within the open solicitation documents and the standardized fillable price list. ***************************************************************************************** SECTION 1.0: GENERAL SOLICITATION INFORMATION 1. title: Design/Build Maintenance and Repair Army Reserve (MRAR) of the Charleston Armed Forces Reserve Center, Building 17001 located in Charleston (Cross Lanes), West Virginia (WV)
description: DESCRIPTION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Louisville District intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) W912QR26RA059 for the Maintenance and Repair Army Reserve (MRAR) of a two-story Armed Forces Reserve Center (AFRC), in Charleston (Cross Lanes), West Virginia. The AFRC includes approximately 56,520 square feet of usable floor space and was originally constructed in 1986. A new roof will be installed prior to the start of this project. The project involves the modernization of an existing AFRC, to include a new elevator, additional access to 2nd floor, new windows, new doors, and complete replacement of HVAC, electric, plumbing, and telecom. individual room controls. Bathrooms will require new fixtures, showers, and toilets. Additional interior improvements may include new or replacement floor coverings, new or replacement wall coverings, and new or replacement ceiling systems. Supporting facilities include paving, general site improvements, and utility connections. Anti-Terrorism/Force Protection (ATFP) and physical security measures have been incorporated into design including maximum standoff distance from roads and parking areas. Sustainability/Energy measures are included. The project will contain the following options: 1) Loading Ramp; 2) Loading Ramp Design Fees; 3) MKT Pad; 4) MKT Pad Design Fees; 5) CFCI OMAR Funded Items; 6) CFCI Bona Fide Need OMAR Funded Items.The Contract Duration is one thousand and two hundred (1,200) calendar days from Contract Notice to Proceed. TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This RFP will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. The North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) for this effort is 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction.This award is Subject to the Availability of Funds (SAF).TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: This acquisition will be a Full and Open. A small business sub-contracting plan will be required prior to award. SELECTION PROCESS: This is a two-phase Design/Build procurement. The proposals will be evaluated using a Best Value Tradeoff source selection process. The technical information contained in each Offerors proposal will be reviewed, evaluated, and rated by the Government. Potential offerors are invited to submit their past performance, technical, and capability information as will be described in Section 00 22 16 and Section 00 22 18 of the Solicitation, for review and consideration by the Government.As will be described in Section 00 22 16 of the Solicitation, the selection process for Phase I will evaluate such factors as Past Performance (for both the Prime Contractor and A/E Designer of Record) and Technical Approach for Design/Build. Pro Forma Information such as bonding and financial capability will also be required to meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation. Following completion of the evaluation of Phase I, a target of five (5) of the most highly qualified offerors will be invited to participate in Phase II. The selected offerors for Phase II will be requested to submit additional information as will be described in Section 00 22 18 of the Solicitation, for review and evaluation by the Government. The selection process for Phase II will evaluate such factors as: Design Narrative, Schedule Narrative, and Price. The Standard Form (SF) 1442 will also be required. (NOTE: The evaluation factors for Phase II are subject to change with the Phase II amendment.) DISCUSSIONS: The Government intends to award without discussions but reserves the right to conduct discussions should it be deemed in the Governments best interest.SOLICITATION WEBSITE: The official solicitation, when posted, will be available free of charge by electronic posting only and may be found at federal Contract Opportunities website, https://sam.gov and the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module website, https://piee.eb.mil/. Paper copies of the solicitation will not be issued. Telephone and Fax requests for this solicitation will not be honored. Project files are Portable Document Format (PDF) files and can be viewed, navigated, or printed using Adobe Acrobat Reader. To download the solicitation for this project, contractors are required to register at the System for Award Management at https://sam.gov. Amendments, if/when issued, will be posted to the above referenced websites for electronic downloading. This will be the only method of distributing amendments prior to closing; therefore, it is the Offerors responsibility to check the websites periodically for any amendments to the solicitation.The solicitation documents can be downloaded by following the PIEE Solicitation Module Link for W912QR26RA059 Link in the Links / Attachments Section below.REGISTRATIONS: Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the following database: System to for Award Management (SAM): Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the SAM database at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for a Government contract award. If the Offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity shall have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. If at the time of award an Offeror is not actively and successfully registered in the SAM database, the Government reserves the right award to the next prospective Offeror.POINT-OF-CONTACT: The point-of-contact for this procurement is Contract Specialist, Mr. Laura Phillips-Payne at Laura.Phillips-Payne@usace.army.milPARTNERING WITH US: https://www.usace.army.mil/Business-With-Us/Partnering/Information regarding the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers process for settling requests for equitable adjustments and duration goals to achieve definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts can be found by going to https://www.usace.army.mil/Business-With-Us/Partnering/ and then clicking on: View FFP Contract Changes Playbook Here.

title: Maintenance, Repair, and Preservation of Edgecumbe Barge
description: 4 AUG 2026: The purpose of this amendment is to update the Attachment 1 Statement of Work as of 4 August 2026 as a result of Request for Clarification (RFC) 01. Government answer to RFC 01 is also posted. _______________________________________________ The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF), Bremerton, Washington intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of one (1) Edgecumbe RCD Barge. The Edgecumbe RCD Barge characteristics are 240 FT length, 60 FT width, 2 FT 11 IN Draft, 928 L Tons full displacement, 48 years of age, and hull material is steel. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of accommodating one (1) Edgecumbe RCD Barge with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the Contracting Officers Representative (COR) to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Accomplish zinc anode replacement; preliminary and final air tests of all tanks/voids; tank/void open, clean and gas free; and support ABS and USCG inspections. Undock the vessel. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the COR. The vessel availability is scheduled to be 1 December 2026 to 23 December 2026. This is full and open competition. All offerors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) to receive award of Government contracts. Offerors are advised also that SAM representations and certifications can be completed electronically via the System for Award Management website at https://www.sam.gov.

title: Dental and Audiology Coordinator for the Vermont Army National Guard
description: This is a non-personal services contract to provide the Vermont Army National Guard (VTARNG) Deputy State Surgeon?s Office (DSS) with professional, non-clinical administrative support services for the Dental Health Program and the Hearing Conservation Program. The strategic objective of this contract is to optimize the medical, dental, and auditory readiness of VTARNG Service Members (SMs) in accordance with Army Regulation (AR) 40-501 (Standards of Medical Fitness) and AR 40-502 (Medical Readiness). The contractor shall deliver independent, highly accurate administrative data entry, records tracking, scheduling, and metrics reporting as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS).Non-Personal Services Framework In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 37.104, this contract is strictly designated as a non-personal services contract. Government Authority and Supervision: The Government shall not exercise any direct supervision, tasking, or administrative control over contractor employees performing services under this contract. Contractor personnel shall remain at all times under the direct supervision, management, and administrative control of the Contractor?s Contract Manager (CM).Contractor Accountability: The Contractor shall be solely responsible for the selection, hiring, oversight, conduct, scheduling, and performance of its personnel. Contractor employees shall be accountable solely to the Contractor, who, in turn, is responsible to the Government for the successful delivery of the outcomes outlined herein. Professional Boundaries: Under no circumstances shall any relationship resembling an employer-employee (co-employment) relationship be established between the Government and contractor personnel. Service Contract Act (SCA) / Service Contract Labor Standards (SCLS) Compliance To maintain regulatory alignment with 41 U.S.C. Chapter 67 (Service Contract Labor Standards) and to prevent labor misclassification or Wage Determination violations: Mandated Labor Classification: Offerors shall utilize the mandatory SCA labor category of Medical Record Clerk (Labor Category Code 12160) to execute all requirements outlined in this PWS. This is strictly for one (1) FTE Medical Records Clerk. Wage and Benefit Floor: All proposed labor rates must strictly conform to or exceed the minimum wage and fringe benefit requirements established in the applicable Department of Labor (DOL) Wage Determination attached to this solicitation. Strictly Administrative Scope: The duties outlined under this contract are exclusively clerical, administrative, and data-driven. The Medical Record Clerk is a non-clinical role. Contractor personnel are strictly prohibited from performing any tasks that require clinical evaluation, medical charting, clinical triage, patient counseling, or the independent authoring of medical/dental opinions. Mandatory Personnel Qualifications. The Contractor shall ensure that all personnel assigned to perform services under this contract possess and maintain, at a minimum, the following mandatory professional qualifications: Professional Experience Healthcare Administration Background: A minimum of two (2) years of demonstrated, hands-on experience in medical or dental administration, medical records management, military health administration, or a related healthcare clerical field. Records Management Proficiency: Proven experience handling sensitive personal data, physical/electronic archiving, and verifying the administrative completeness of standardized medical/dental intake documentation. Technical and Computer Skills Microsoft Office Suite: Demonstrated high-level proficiency in using the Microsoft Office Suite, specifically: Microsoft Excel: Ability to manage spreadsheets, utilize basic formulas, and organize data for weekly metrics reporting. Microsoft Word: Ability to draft professional administrative correspondence and schedules. Microsoft Outlook: Ability to coordinate scheduling and professional communication across secure email networks. Systems Adaptability: Proven capability to quickly learn and perform high-accuracy data entry within proprietary military and federal web-based databases (including but not limited to MEDCHART, eCase, DENCLASS, and MEDPROS) following initial Government-provided systems training. Security and Information Assurance Clearance: Federal Clearability: All personnel must be U.S. citizens and must be capable of successfully passing a federal Tier 1 background investigation (formerly National Agency Check with Inquiries - NACI) to secure a Common Access Card (CAC) for physical installation access and logical access to secure military networks. Data Privacy Competency: Prior experience handling Protected Health Information (PHI) and Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in strict compliance with HIPAA, HITECH, and military privacy regulations. Prerequisite for Award: To be considered for award, quoters must have a current NIST SP 800-171 Basic Assessment score posted in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) at the exact time of quote submission. The Government will verify SPRS records immediately following the submission deadline. Failure to have a verified, active score in SPRS at the time of quote submission shall result in the quote being determined non-responsive and immediately disqualified from further evaluation. No grace periods, updates, or post-submission self-assessments will be accepted. Quoters are required to ask questions NLT 16 August 2026. Questions received after that date will not be answered or posted. Questions and answers will be posted with 48 hours of receipt.

description: UPDATE: August 7, 2026 NASA is actively working to finalize and publish responses to all questions and comments submitted under the Appendix B solicitation and Direct-Topic Call 1. Due to the significant level of industry engagement, and to better support offerors, NASA will release these responses in batches as they are completed. UPDATE: July 16, 2026 The final solicitation for Next Space Technologies for Exploration Partnerships-3 (NextSTEP-3), Appendix B, Moon to Mars Architectural Studies, issued under solicitation number 80MSFC26R0003, has been reissued as Appendix B: Moon Base Demonstrations and supersedes previous solicitation instructions. In December 2025, a national space policy was signed into place that emphasized America's leadership in space, including returning to the Moon, building a permanent base, investing in new technologies, and advancing lunar and orbital economies for future scientific missions. NASA�s Moon Base, located in the lunar South Pole region, will serve as the premier proving ground for deep space exploration, empowering scientific discovery and the development of advanced space technologies. Based on the preceding, Appendix B will now focus on phased implementation of Moon Base. NASA seeks to bridge the gap between technology development and mission operations, targeting concepts at technology readiness level (TRL) 6 and beyond. Industry partners play a critical role in addressing architectural gaps and risk reduction buy-down that create the knowledge foundation NASA needs to make informed programmatic decisions and strengthen its ability to achieve strategic exploration goals efficiently and effectively. To that end, NASA's Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate (HSMD) is actively embracing innovative ideas from industry partners through this Appendix B: Moon Base Demonstrations under the NextSTEP-3 Omnibus Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) that calls for industry-led demonstrations and special topic activities. This BAA uses a dual-path call structure: Directed-Topic Calls and Open-Topic Calls. NASA will periodically release specific Directed-Topic Calls to guide industry partners and promote focused innovation in support of Moon Base objectives. These Directed-Topic Calls are designed to address evolving mission needs and encourage proposals that advance technologies and capabilities critical to lunar exploration. NASA intends to also have Open-Topic Calls available at a later date to allow industry to propose concepts within the topics outlined above that are not part of any prior Directed-Topic Calls included within this announcement. Open opportunities are meant to capture innovative solutions from the broader industrial base and may result in a contract to any qualified organization. Open-Topic submissions with identical concepts as Directed-Topic Calls will not be evaluated. This announcement will follow a 2-step process for proposal submissions. Step-1 of the process is the submission of a White Paper. In Step-2 of the process, only invited proposers will be requested to submit a full project proposal. NASA intends to award Firm-Fixed Price contracts with performance-based milestone payments. All awards will be subject to the provisions of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and the NASA FAR Supplement (NFS). All questions regarding this solicitation should be submitted in writing, electronically to Brad Vest, Contracting Officer, at Bradley.D.Vest@nasa.gov no later than 5:00 p.m., Central Time (CT), July 30, 2026. Offerors are encouraged to submit questions as soon as possible for consideration. The Offeror shall courtesy copy (cc) hq-nextstep3appb@mail.nasa.gov on this communication. ________________________________________________________________________ The final solicitation for Next Space Technologies for Exploration Partnerships-3 (NextSTEP-3), Appendix B, Moon to Mars Architectural Studies, issued under solicitation number 80MSFC26R0003, is on hold until further notice. title: Decentralized Artificial Intelligence through Controlled Emergence (DICE)
description: The DICE program seeks to develop the theory and algorithms for decentralized coordination and local inference control to enable a scalable, adaptive, and resilient collective of heterogeneous AI agents that can autonomously execute sustained long-time-horizon missions in contested environments while remaining under human control. In contrast to small-scale, rigid, and fragile centralized orchestration or the high-risk unpredictable nature of ad hoc compositions of AI agents, DICE aims to harness the scalability and adaptability of self-organizing systems while minimizing risks and ensuring that the collective behavior remains predictable and aligned with intended outcomes. This approach mirrors the principles of decentralized self-organization that underpin the internet's own scalability and resilience, where robust global behavior emerges from simple, local rules.

title: ASL interpreter
description: Introduction & Background The Naval Health Clinic (NBHC) Portsmouth is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing on-site/in-person American Sign Language (ASL) interpretive services on an as-needed basis. These services are required to support Deaf and/or Hard of Hearing individuals assigned to NBHC Portsmouth, NH. The primary scope of support is for the Industrial Hygiene department. Support encompasses both traditional office environments and dynamic survey work executed across the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, the NBHC Portsmouth Area of Responsibility (AOR), and remote locations across Northern New England. Scope of Work & Key Requirements Interested vendors must demonstrate the capability to meet the logistical, administrative, and environmental demands of this requirement. The contractor must provide seamless sign-to-voice and voice-to-sign ASL interpretive services. From a scheduling perspective, vendors must be capable of receiving service requests by 1500 the day prior to the event and providing positive confirmation to the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) no later than 1800 the same day. Punctuality and accountability are paramount to this requirement. Personnel must arrive at the NAVMEDREADTRNUNIT PORTSMOUTH Industrial Hygiene office 30 minutes prior to the scheduled start time for COR check-in, and execute a proper check-out upon completion or early release. Furthermore, the contractor must maintain a zero-tolerance policy for cancellations and no-shows, demonstrating the capacity to immediately provide backfill ASL interpreters if the primary interpreter is unavailable. For field operations, personnel supporting industrial hygiene surveys and exposure monitoring must be physically capable of traversing active industrial work areas. Vendors must supply their personnel with all required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), including safety shoes or boots, hard hats, safety glasses, and up to double hearing protection. Conversely, personnel supporting standard office and training events must maintain a neat, clean, and professional appearance, conducting themselves in accordance with military installation standards at all times. Capability Statement Instructions Interested parties are requested to submit a Capability Statement demonstrating their ability to fulfill the requirements outlined above. Submissions must include a comprehensive company profile detailing the Company Name, CAGE Code, UEI Number, Point of Contact, and applicable Business Size standard. Respondents should also provide examples of past performance involving similar ASL services provided within the last three years, preferably in industrial, shipyard, or military healthcare environments. Additionally, the statement must contain a brief narrative explaining how the company manages rapid deployment, day-before scheduling, and emergency backfill procedures to guarantee zero no-shows. Finally, vendors must confirm their ability to supply ASL interpreters with the necessary PPE for heavy industrial environments.

title: East Access Road Repairs at Union Village Dam, Thetford, VT
description: Union Village Dam, Thetford, VT ??????????????????????????? East Access Road RepairsThe U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing a set aside for certified small business contractors for the East Access Road Repairs at the Union Village Dam in Thetford, Vermont. The NAICS code for the work described below is 237310 with a size standard of $45M. The period of performance will be 365 days. The estimated magnitude of this project is between $350,000 and $700,000 The work of this project involves reconstructing and repairing of a segment of the existing gravel road and a segment of the existing asphalt paved road, a riprap-lined roadside drainage ditch at a location on Buzzell Bridge Road, just east of the Union Village Dam in Thetford, Vermont is also included. The project includes an option bid item to complete the removal and disposal of existing asphalt pavement and the full depth hot mix asphalt replacement to the remaining asphalt paved road. As part of the base bid, the work will also include the full removal and offsite disposal of an existing large diameter pipe culvert with plastic flared end and the existing concrete drop inlet structure.The work also includes the installation of a new precast reinforced concrete box culvert, new precast reinforced concrete headwalls and wingwalls at the inlet and outlet ends of the new culvert and a new energy dissipator at the outlet end of the new culvert consisting of a rock riprap-lined stilling basin and rock riprap apron. Work will also include clearing and grubbing of trees and their offsite disposal, the removal and disposal of washed out, broken, and cracked existing asphalt pavement and removal silty subgrade soils, the removal, stockpiling, and reuse of existing 18-inch (d50) rock riprap, cleaning and re-adjustment to three existing concrete drop inlet structures and their plastic pipe culverts.The work will also include all necessary earthwork, such as, but not limited to excavation, filling, backfilling, trenching, compaction, and grading; placing topsoil and seeding at disturbed areas; and the placement, maintenance, inspection, and removal of erosion prevention and sedimentation controls measures.Please note that this solicitation is set aside for certified small businesses. Neither telephonic, mailed, nor faxed requests for hard copies of this solicitation will be accepted. The solicitation will only be available online; in order to view the solicitation offerors must access the System for Award Management website (www.sam.gov). In order to download the solicitation, bidders must access the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (https://piee.eb.mil/). All responsible sources may submit a bid which shall be considered by the USACE New England District.
